notes: Follow-up release that fixes the in-app wordmark quality regression introduced by v1.0.37 and inherited by v1.0.38. The user reported the dashboard / login / onboarding / admin / Tauri-splash wordmark "looks like Roblox shit, not AI level work" — the auto-traced vector geometry that v1.0.37 produced via vtracer (and v1.0.38 inherited verbatim) gave rough/blocky letterforms that did not match the polished Copilot reference (`branding/png/wordmark-master.png`). The geometry was the problem, not the file format: auto-tracers like potrace/vtracer can never reproduce the subtle shading + gradient detail of a finished raster, so any vector trace of the master will always look like an approximation of the original. v1.0.39 reverts the in-app wordmark from SVG back to PNG and ships three pixel densities (`@1x` / `@2x` / `@3x`) so the browser picks the matching asset for the user's display DPI — the same `` pattern Apple, Google, Microsoft, and Stripe ship for their brand wordmarks. No functional changes for the trading engine. This is a normal point release — both v1.0.38 and v1.0.39 share the `com.asasystems.terminal` Tauri identifier, so v1.0.38 users update via the in-app updater the same way every other point release lands. No manual install required. ### Brand assets - **In-app wordmark switched from auto-traced SVG (v1.0.37/38) to high-DPI PNG with `srcset` (v1.0.39).** v1.0.37 ran `vtracer` against `branding/png/wordmark-master.png` (1536×1024 Copilot-generated raster) to produce `branding/svg/asa-wordmark-vectorized.svg`, and v1.0.38 unified the green shades inside that trace to phosphor #5FFF7E. The trace was geometrically *close* but the letterforms read as rough/blocky in-app: the chevron A's lost their flat-cut apex sharpness, the S fold corners gained jagged step artifacts, and the whole wordmark looked like a cartoon outline of the brand mark rather than the brand mark itself. There is no clean vector hidden inside a polished raster — the master has anti-aliased edges, subtle gradient shading, and refined corner rounding that any tracer either over-segments or smooths away. v1.0.39 abandons auto-tracing for the in-app wordmark and re-sources directly from the master raster: `scripts/build_wordmark_pngs.py` reads `branding/png/wordmark-master.png`, tightly crops the wordmark bounding box (drops the ~30% dark padding that the Copilot raster includes around the mark), then emits six PNGs — three densities × two themes — via PIL Lanczos resize plus a mild unsharp mask (`radius=0.6, percent=80, threshold=2`, comparable to ImageMagick `-unsharp 0x0.5`). The on-dark variant carries the original Copilot colours (white A's, original folded-S green, charcoal background); the on-light variant is built by detecting the green pixels via channel-dominance + brightness thresholding (kept untouched), recolouring the white A pixels to charcoal #1A1C1F, and replacing the dark background with cream #FAFAF7 — all inside the same source image so the geometry is byte-identical between themes. - **Three densities ship at 400 / 800 / 1200 px wide.** A 200 px display footprint (the natural size for the dashboard sidebar wordmark) renders crisp at 1× DPI from the 400-px asset, at 2× DPI from the 800-px asset, and at 3× DPI / 4K from the 1200-px asset. The browser's `srcset` resolver picks the matching density automatically based on `window.devicePixelRatio`, so a Windows machine running at 175% DPI scaling lands on `@2x` (the closest match above 1.75×) and a 4K external monitor at 200% DPI lands on `@2x` exactly. Output sizes: `wordmark-on-dark@1x.png` 26 KB, `@2x.png` 78 KB, `@3x.png` 133 KB; `wordmark-on-light@1x.png` 21 KB, `@2x.png` 60 KB, `@3x.png` 106 KB. Total weight under 425 KB across all six PNGs vs the previous single 14 KB SVG, but the resolver only loads the picked density per visit. - **`` plumbing across five surfaces.** `dashboard.html`, `templates/login.html`, `templates/onboarding.html`, `templates/admin.html` each replace their `` line with the three-density `` pattern. The dashboard's light-theme override in `static/css/components.css` switches from `content: url("…wordmark-header-on-light.svg")` to the CSS-equivalent `content: image-set(url("…wordmark-on-light@1x.png") 1x, url("…@2x.png") 2x, url("…@3x.png") 3x)` so the light theme also gets density resolution rather than falling back to a single fixed-resolution PNG. The `image-rendering: -webkit-optimize-contrast` hint that previous versions toggled in/out is replaced by `image-rendering: auto` everywhere — the browser's bicubic smoothing produces a better result than nearest-neighbour or `optimize-contrast` when the picked density needs sub-pixel adjustment to fill the display CSS px footprint. - **Tauri splash uses the same three-density import.** `tray-app/src/App.tsx` was previously importing a single SVG (`./assets/wordmark-header.svg`); v1.0.39 imports the three PNG densities (`./assets/wordmark-on-dark@1x.png`, `@2x.png`, `@3x.png`), composes them into a `srcSet` string at module scope, and renders ``. Vite's client types in `vite-env.d.ts` already declare default-export URL strings for `*.png` so no build config changes were needed. The splash webview uses the same DPI-resolution path as the Flask-served dashboard surfaces, so the wordmark rendering is consistent from cold-start splash through to authenticated dashboard. - **`branding/svg/asa-wordmark-vectorized.svg` and the v1.0.38-derived `wordmark-header.svg` / `wordmark-header-on-light.svg` files are kept on disk** — the marketing landing page (out of scope for this release) and the brand-spec HTML still reference them. The five in-app surfaces no longer touch any SVG wordmark asset. ### Visual diff Side-by-side comparison of the new `wordmark-on-dark@2x.png` rendered at 200 px wide vs the Copilot reference master rendered at 200 px wide is saved at `scripts/_v1039_visual_diff_200px.png` for the build record. Letterforms match 1:1 — same chevron A apex angle, same S fold corner geometry, same colour saturation. The only visible difference is that the new asset fills the 200 px container edge-to-edge (the tight crop removed the master's 30% padding), which is the desired outcome for the dashboard sidebar where every pixel of horizontal real estate matters. ### Auto-updater note Same shipping pipeline as v1.0.30 → v1.0.38: PyInstaller `server.exe` sidecar → Tauri NSIS bundle → manual minisign with `npx tauri signer sign -f - -p ""` from bash (NOT auto-signer in PowerShell pipes — that produces 0-byte sigs) → SHA256 + UTF-8-no-BOM `latest.json` → `gh release create` → uploaded to `cjml34483/TradeSpace-releases`. v1.0.38 → v1.0.39 auto-updates cleanly because the Tauri identifier (`com.asasystems.terminal`) is unchanged.
